sources.title: Learning to Give Checkable Answers with Prover-Verifier Games — quoted full-text passages (arXiv 2108.12099v1 PDF)

state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: The authors show (Theorem 4) that under the simultaneous game formulation, from any initialization with all message probabilities positive, gradient descent on both players with reasonable learning rates converges to the prover sending message 1 only when x = 1 and the verifier predicting 1 only on message 1, up to a small constant set by entropy regularization; in the sequential formulation where the prover plays first (Theorem 5), gradient descent with any learning rates converges to the prover sending only messages 2 to K regardless of input, an undesirable solution.
title: PVG: gradient descent finds protocol when simultaneous, not prover-first
